title: A First-Timer's K-Beauty & Shopping Tour of Seoul: 2 Nights, 3 Days Itinerary
html:
If your Korea trip is built around skincare, makeup, and a suitcase with room to spare, this 2 nights, 3 days route is for you. Seoul has three very different ways to shop tax-free — and they're easy to mix up as a first-timer. This guide walks you through all three (instant tax refunds, downtown duty-free, and airport duty-free) so you don't accidentally leave money — or your shopping bags — behind.

Like the rest of this blog's itineraries, this one assumes you're staying somewhere central (Myeongdong, Hongdae, or City Hall all work) and have a T-money transit card — a rechargeable card sold at any convenience store, used for subways, buses, and even some taxis.

Day 1: Myeongdong — Cosmetics Street & Instant Tax Refunds

Myeongdong (Myeongdong Station, Line 4, Exit 6) is Seoul's best-known beauty shopping street — a few blocks packed almost entirely with skincare and makeup shops. Your main stop should be Olive Young, Korea's biggest beauty retail chain (think a huge, multi-floor drugstore stocked with hundreds of Korean skincare and makeup brands). Myeongdong actually has several Olive Young branches within a few minutes of each other, including the large "Myeongdong Town" global flagship and a newer, even bigger "Central Myeongdong Town" store that opened in March 2026 with AI-powered skin analysis machines and English-speaking staff on every floor.

Here's the beginner-friendly part: at Olive Young's Myeongdong and Hongdae branches, if you spend ₩15,000 or more on one receipt, just show your passport at checkout and the roughly 10% tax is taken off immediately — no separate refund counter, no paperwork to mail in. This works for purchases up to ₩1,000,000 per receipt. (A few items, like sanitary products, don't qualify — the cashier will tell you if something's excluded.) At smaller shops that don't offer instant refunds, ask for a tax-refund receipt and use one of the self-service refund kiosks scattered around Myeongdong before you leave the area.

One of Myeongdong's cosmetics shopping streets. Photo: SKTakek, CC0 (public domain), via Wikimedia Commons.

Between stores, graze on Myeongdong's street food stalls — this is one of the easiest places in Seoul to try things like tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes) or Korean-style rolled egg toast without committing to a sit-down meal.

Day 2: Department Stores, Downtown Duty-Free & Dongdaemun Night Market

Spend today on bigger purchases. Lotte Department Store (Main branch + the younger-skewing Young Plaza next door) and Shinsegae Department Store Main Branch — Korea's oldest department store building, still in use — both sit within walking distance in Myeongdong. These are regular retail stores (not duty-free), but each has a tourist information desk and tax-refund counter, so the same instant or receipt-based refund from Day 1 applies here too.

For genuinely bigger savings, this is also where you'll find downtown duty-free stores — Lotte Duty Free's Myeongdong Main Store and Shinsegae Duty Free Myeongdong. Duty-free is different from a tax refund: prices are already both tax- and tariff-free at the register, so the discount is bigger, especially on perfume, liquor, and imported luxury brands. The catch, and the thing that trips up first-timers: for most imported brands, you don't get to carry your purchase out of the store. You'll get a pickup slip instead, and collect the actual items at a duty-free pickup counter at the airport on your departure day (more on that below). The one exception is Korean brands like Sulwhasoo or Whoo — those you can usually take with you right away.

In the evening, head to Dongdaemun for a completely different shopping style. Malls like Doota stay open very late into the night, have no minimum purchase, and are packed floor after floor with Korean streetwear, accessories, and up-and-coming local designer brands — a fun, low-pressure way to browse after a heavier shopping day.

Doota, one of Dongdaemun's late-night fashion malls. Photo: Tim (mullenkedheim), CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Day 3: Outlet Day Trip (Optional) & Duty-Free Pickup Before You Fly

If you still have energy — and suitcase space — for international fashion brands at outlet prices, consider a half-day trip to Paju Premium Outlets. It's reachable by regular public bus: Bus 2200 from Hongik University Station (Exit 11), about a 40-minute ride for roughly ₩2,500 — no advance booking required, so it's easy to slot in on a whim. Yeoju Premium Outlets is bigger (270+ brands) but only reachable by a paid round-trip shuttle that runs a few set days a week and needs booking in advance through a site like Klook or KKday — worth it if outlet shopping is the main point of your day, less so as a quick add-on.

Whether or not you go to an outlet, save time on your last day for duty-free pickup. Head to the duty-free pickup zone at Incheon Airport (Terminal 1, 2nd floor, or Terminal 2, 3rd floor) after you've checked in and passed security. Scan your passport at the kiosk, take a number, and wait to be called — during busy periods this can take 30–60 minutes, so don't leave it for the last 20 minutes before boarding. As of 2026, Lotte Duty Free and Hyundai Duty Free run the airport's main cosmetics and perfume counters, so if you still need a last souvenir or forgot something, you can also buy directly at the airport (no pickup needed for on-the-spot airport purchases).

A Lotte Duty Free shop at Incheon International Airport. Photo: Vuong Tri Binh, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

What Locals Actually Do

Tourists tend to funnel into the biggest, busiest Olive Young flagship store in Myeongdong — but locals usually shop at a smaller neighborhood branch a few minutes away, where the shelves are just as stocked and there's no line for the register. If the Myeongdong flagship looks packed, it's often faster (and just as good) to walk one block over to a quieter branch.

Which Tax-Free Option Should You Use?

OptionWhereWhen you get the discountWhen you get the itemBest for
Instant tax refundOlive Young (Myeongdong/Hongdae), some other shopsAt checkoutImmediatelyEveryday beauty shopping, ₩15,000+ receipts
Downtown duty-freeLotte/Shinsegae Duty Free, MyeongdongAt checkout (already tax/tariff-free)Airport pickup (Korean brands: immediately)Perfume, liquor, luxury, imported brands
Airport duty-freeIncheon Airport, after securityAt checkoutImmediatelyLast-minute or forgotten items

meta_description: A beginner's 2N3D Seoul shopping itinerary covering Myeongdong's cosmetics street, Olive Young instant refunds, department stores, downtown duty-free, Dongdaemun, and outlet day trips.
